options: An electrostatic charge pattern created by the laser
items.answer: An electrostatic charge pattern created by the laser
items.markingKey: The laser discharges areas of the charged drum; charged toner sticks to the pattern, is transferred to paper and fused by heat.

items.stem: Explain why an SSD is more suitable than a hard disk drive for a laptop.

items.stem: Describe how a laser printer produces a printed page.
items.answer: The drum is given a charge; a laser removes charge where the image is not wanted (or creates the image pattern); toner is attracted to the charged areas; toner is transferred to charged paper; the fuser melts the toner onto the paper; the drum is discharged.
items.markingKey: 1 mark per correct stage in sequence, max 4 [4]

items.stem: In a hard disk drive, what moves to position the read/write head over the correct track?
items.answer: The actuator arm
items.markingKey: Platters spin; the actuator arm moves the head across tracks; data stored as magnetised regions.

items.stem: Answer both parts. (a) Describe how a speaker produces sound from a digital file. (b) Explain why an SSD is more suitable than a hard disk drive for a laptop.
items.answer: (a) A DAC converts the digital data to an analogue signal; the varying current flows through the coil, creating a changing magnetic field; the coil and cone move in and out, creating sound waves. (b) No moving parts so more robust if dropped; faster access; lighter and uses less power, so better battery life.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark: DAC; 1 mark: current in coil/magnetic field; 1 mark: cone vibrates producing pressure waves [3] (b) 1 mark per point, max 3 [3]

items.stem: Explain your reasoning in each part. (a) Describe how a laser printer produces a printed page. (b) Explain why an SSD can wear out over time.
items.answer: (a) The drum is given a charge; a laser removes charge where the image is not wanted (or creates the image pattern); toner is attracted to the charged areas; toner is transferred to charged paper; the fuser melts the toner onto the paper; the drum is discharged. (b) Flash memory cells can only be written/erased a limited number of times before they fail.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark per correct stage in sequence, max 4 [4] (b) 1 mark: limited write/erase cycles; 1 mark: cells degrade [2]

items.stem: A school in Nairobi is buying hardware for a technology classroom. Explain why the computers should be fitted with SSDs rather than HDDs.
items.answer: Faster boot and file access; no moving parts so more reliable; quieter.
items.markingKey: 1 mark per point, max 2 [2]

items.stem: A portable drive has a capacity of 4 TB. Each of the songs to be stored is 10 MB. Calculate how many songs can be stored (1 TB = 1,000,000 MB).

items.stem: The IT manager at SkyLink Airways has been asked to prepare a recommendation. Assess the replacement of all hard disk drives with solid-state drives in the computers at SkyLink Airways.
items.answer: Points in favour: faster access and boot times; no moving parts so robust; lower power and heat; silent. Points against / limitations: higher cost per GB; limited write cycles; data recovery after failure is harder; existing HDDs still work. Conclusion: SSDs for operating system and active work, HDD/tape for bulk archives is a common compromise.

items.stem: Orbit Games Studio in Istanbul is reviewing its hardware budget. Evaluate the use of 3D printers by Orbit Games Studio to make spare parts on demand.
items.answer: Points in favour: parts made quickly when needed; less stock held; custom designs; less transport. Conclusion: suitable for small runs and rare parts, not mass production.

items.stem: How is an EPROM erased?
options: By applying a voltage while in the circuit
By exposing it to ultraviolet light
By deleting files in the OS
items.answer: By exposing it to ultraviolet light
items.markingKey: EPROM: erased with UV light through a quartz window; EEPROM: erased electrically.

items.stem: Assertion (A): SRAM is cheaper per gigabyte than DRAM. Reason (R): EEPROM can be erased and rewritten electrically. Which option is correct?
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
items.answer: A is false but R is true
items.markingKey: A is false: "SRAM is cheaper per gigabyte than DRAM." is incorrect; R is a true statement.

items.stem: Answer both parts. (a) Explain why SRAM does not need refreshing but DRAM does. (b) Explain why a manufacturer of washing machines might use EEPROM rather than ROM for the control program.
items.answer: (a) SRAM stores each bit in a flip-flop that holds its state while powered; DRAM stores a bit as charge on a capacitor that leaks away. (b) The firmware can be updated electrically in the field to fix bugs or add features without replacing the chip.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark: SRAM flip-flops; 1 mark: DRAM capacitors leak [2] (b) 1 mark: can be reprogrammed/updated; 1 mark: without removing/replacing chip [2]

items.stem: Sipho is choosing the memory for a new laptop to be sold by SwiftCar Rentals. Explain why adding more RAM can improve performance.
items.answer: More programs/data held in RAM so less use of virtual memory (swapping to disk), which is slow.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: less virtual memory/paging; 1 mark: disk access slower than RAM [2]

items.stem: Sofia is choosing the memory for a new laptop to be sold by Horizon Travel. Explain why the device uses a small amount of SRAM as well as DRAM.
items.answer: SRAM is fast so used as cache for frequently used data; DRAM is cheap for large main memory.

items.stem: Starlight Cinemas in Jakarta is designing a new games console with RAM, ROM and cache memory. (a) Explain why adding more RAM can improve performance. (b) Suggest why EEPROM is better than PROM for the firmware.
items.answer: (a) More programs/data held in RAM so less use of virtual memory (swapping to disk), which is slow. (b) Firmware updates/bug fixes can be installed later; PROM can only be written once.

items.stem: Ravi is writing a buying guide that explains computer memory. (a) Compare SRAM and DRAM in terms of speed, cost and density. (b) Explain the role of ROM in the start-up of the device.
items.answer: (a) SRAM faster, more expensive, lower density; DRAM slower, cheaper, higher density. (b) ROM holds the bootstrap/BIOS which tests hardware and loads the OS from storage into RAM.

items.stem: Answer both parts. (a) Why are buffers used when streaming video? (b) What is a buffer?
items.answer: (a) To store data in advance so playback continues smoothly if the download rate varies (b) A temporary memory area that holds data being transferred between devices
items.markingKey: (a) The buffer is filled ahead of playback; the player reads from it at a steady rate. (b) Buffers compensate for differences in speed between devices (e.g. CPU and printer).

items.stem: Explain your reasoning in each part. (a) Explain how a buffer is used when a document is sent from a computer to a printer. (b) Give two advantages and one disadvantage of embedded systems.
items.answer: (a) Data is sent to the printer buffer at high speed; the printer reads it at its own slower speed; the CPU can continue other tasks; when the buffer is empty an interrupt requests more data. (b) Advantages: small, cheap to mass-produce, low power, reliable/dedicated, fast response. Disadvantage: difficult to upgrade; limited user interface; hard to repair.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark per point, max 3 [3] (b) 1 mark per point, max 3 [3]

items.stem: Answer both parts. (a) Give two advantages and one disadvantage of embedded systems. (b) Explain why embedded systems are often programmed in firmware stored in ROM or flash memory.
items.answer: (a) Advantages: small, cheap to mass-produce, low power, reliable/dedicated, fast response. Disadvantage: difficult to upgrade; limited user interface; hard to repair. (b) The program must be available immediately at power-on and rarely changes; non-volatile memory keeps it without power.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark per point, max 3 [3] (b) 1 mark: non-volatile; 1 mark: fixed dedicated function [2]
